answer: At dawn each epoch holds one ceremony: every identity joins the ten-minute window, answers prompts live, and is logged on a basalt roster. One presence signs one record, so one operator cannot cover two identities; proctors wander, spot-checking answers. Each fake needs a stand-in: the k-th fake costs 40 credits plus a 50-credit bond, so 1,000 fakes cost 40,000 in fees with 50,000 at risk. An honest agent pays no fee, only its refundable bond. A stand-in rental ring fails when rented answers drift from work history or match another attendee: flagged identities lose bond and standing.
